GraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale:
The predecessor search change did exactly what its feasibility gate was meant to do: it discovered that Worldline's multi-installation model was observable but not explicitly invokable. Instead of hiding that platform gap behind a search-specific router or lifecycle trick, execution stopped and the kernel gained a generic InstallationId-targeting primitive.
This replan therefore does not redesign search. It resumes the same browser service architecture on top of the now-applied platform primitive. Search is still a target-resolution capability, not navigation; CEF still owns only browser-engine primitives; search preferences remain external product/profile policy; and multiple installations of one provider definition remain ordinary plugin runtime composition.
GraceChangeDesignContext.ArchitectureSketch: shell / command surface / agent | | already-classified search text v browser.search/resolve capability handle | | CapabilityTarget::Installation(InstallationId) v generic InvocationBroker | | resolves current live RuntimeId + normal authority admission v selected worldline-browser-search installation | | returns bounded SearchNavigationTarget (data only) v caller separately invokes browser.navigate | v BrowserEngineProvider / CEF

KeyDesignDecisions.Decision: The applied kernel targeting primitive is a mechanism, not preference policy. Search-specific defaults and durable user preference must not be added to worldline-kernel as part of this replan.
Explicit routing is by durable InstallationId. RuntimeId remains ephemeral evidence resolved at invocation time and is never a user/profile selection key.
Target unavailability is fail-closed and never silently falls back to another search installation. This preserves caller intent and avoids confused-deputy/provider-substitution behavior.
`browser.search/0.1` remains a resolve capability returning a navigation target. It does not navigate and does not inherit NavigatePage authority.
The future shell owns address/search/command classification and may store a preferred search InstallationId. The search provider receives only input already classified as search text.
The first provider remains installation-configurable rather than vendor- specific. Two installations of the same definition with different base URL configuration are the proving topology.
Search URL construction remains structural: fixed parsed origin/path, one validated query parameter, bounded static parameters, and user text only as a URL-library-encoded parameter value.
Search query text is sensitive payload. Generic runtime audit may identify capability, InstallationId, resolved RuntimeId, timing and outcome, but not copy the query body by default.

WhyNotAlternatives.Alternative: Search-specific router plugin: rejected because the platform now directly supports exact installation targeting and a router would duplicate generic routing semantics.
One-active-provider lifecycle cardinality: rejected because it artificially weakens Worldline's multi-installation model and turns selection into process lifecycle manipulation.
Kernel preferred-provider table: rejected because preference/default state is product/profile policy rather than microkernel mechanism.
RuntimeId targeting: rejected because RuntimeId is destroyed and replaced on restart, crash, update or replacement.
Silent fallback to AnyCompatible: rejected because explicit selection would stop being explicit and could disclose a query to a different provider.

SecurityAndPrivacy.Point: InstallationId targeting is routing data, not authority.
The caller still needs explicit search-resolution authority before query disclosure.
The returned URL is data and does not bypass normal browser.navigate admission.
Query-derived bytes cannot influence scheme, credentials, hostname or path in the first provider implementation.
Search failure or provider quarantine must not affect direct navigation or unrelated browser services.
Acceptance evidence must verify generic trajectory/runtime records remain payload-free with respect to raw query text.

GraceChangeDesignContext.ProviderSelectionModel:
The proving topology is two simultaneously active installations of `worldline-browser-search`, both exposing the same `browser.search/0.1` capability but owning different loopback provider configuration. The consumer carries or receives an InstallationId chosen by external composition/profile policy and requests that exact installation through the generic kernel targeting primitive. No consumer branch on Google/Yandex/DuckDuckGo or any concrete provider crate is permitted.
Provider provenance comes from kernel-owned invocation metadata: requested InstallationId plus resolved RuntimeId. The search result does not self-assert an authoritative provider identity.
GraceChangeDesignContext.TestingModel:
S3E uses two loopback configurations. Resolving through installation A or B must produce distinct expected targets with zero origin hits. The test then separately invokes normal browser navigation with the returned target and verifies exactly one expected origin request and decoded query value.
The real Windows variant uses staged pinned CEF and the native provider process. Search still executes above CEF; CEF receives only the ordinary navigation target after a separate browser.navigate admission. Reference backend substitution is rejected.
GraceChangeDesignContext.LifecycleReplan: C-BROWSER-SEARCH-PROVIDERS-20260904 remains the stopped predecessor whose T-001 evidence discovered the platform gap. This replacement bundle should be approved before the predecessor is transitioned to superseded/archive state. The replacement exact plan should reuse the original functional tasks where valid but replace the old feasibility gate with a baseline-conformance task proving the already-applied InstallationId targeting primitive in the Search composition.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: Exact persistent storage for the user's preferred search InstallationId belongs to a later Shell/profile change.
Seed provider presets and product default vendor remain configuration/product policy.
Remote suggestions/autocomplete remain a separate capability with their own privacy and cancellation semantics.
Structured search results, workspace retrieval and AI answers remain separate capability families.
